raw_text:
# 12-Week Training & Nutrition Programme

**Client Profile:** Female, 45, Type 2 Diabetic (Metformin, HbA1c 7.2)
**Primary Goals:** Fat loss, improved glycaemic control, increased insulin sensitivity
**Access:** Full gym

---

## Key Diabetic Considerations Up Front

Before getting into the programme, a few non-negotiables to brief her on:

- **Blood glucose monitoring:** She should test pre- and post-training for the first 2-3 weeks to learn how her body responds. Target pre-training: 5.5-13.9 mmol/L (100-250 mg/dL). If below 5.5, have 15g fast carbs before training.
- **Hypo kit:** Glucose tabs/juice in her gym bag at all times.
- **Metformin & training:** Generally well-tolerated, but GI side effects can flare with intense training on an empty stomach. Schedule sessions 1.5-2 hours after a meal where possible.
- **Foot care:** Diabetic neuropathy risk — proper footwear, daily foot checks, no barefoot training.
- **Hydration:** Hyperglycaemia accelerates dehydration. Aim for 2.5-3L water daily.
- **GP clearance:** Confirm she has medical clearance for moderate-to-vigorous exercise and ask about any retinopathy (avoids heavy Valsalva/inversions if present).
- **Quarterly HbA1c retesting** with her GP — we want to see this drop into the 6s by week 12.

---

## Programme Structure Overview

| Phase | Weeks | Focus |
|-------|-------|-------|
| **Phase 1: Foundation** | 1–4 | Movement quality, baseline conditioning, habit formation |
| **Phase 2: Build** | 5–8 | Increased load, metabolic conditioning, glycaemic stress |
| **Phase 3: Intensify** | 9–12 | Higher density, HIIT integration, body recomposition push |

**Weekly Training Split (all phases):**
- 3x Full-body resistance training (Mon/Wed/Fri)
- 2x Cardio sessions (Tue/Sat) — type/intensity progresses per phase
- 1x Mobility/walking active recovery (Thu or Sun)
- Daily step target progresses from 7,000 → 10,000

---

# PHASE 1: FOUNDATION (Weeks 1–4)

Goal: Build movement competency, establish post-meal walking habit (huge for glycaemic control), and get her comfortable with the gym. Resistance training with moderate loads, focus on technique.

### Resistance Session A (Mon & Fri)
- Goblet squat — 3 x 10
- DB chest press — 3 x 10
- Cable row — 3 x 12
- DB Romanian deadlift — 3 x 10
- Dead bug — 3 x 8/side
- Farmer's carry — 3 x 30m

### Resistance Session B (Wed)
- Trap-bar deadlift (or DB deadlift) — 3 x 8
- DB shoulder press — 3 x 10
- Lat pulldown — 3 x 12
- Walking lunges — 3 x 10/side
- Side plank — 3 x 20 sec/side
- Pallof press — 3 x 10/side

Rest 60-90 sec between sets. RPE 6-7.

### Cardio Sessions
- **Tue:** 30 min steady-state (treadmill incline walk or bike) — RPE 5-6, conversational pace
- **Sat:** 30 min steady-state, alternate modality (rower, elliptical)

### Active Recovery (Thu or Sun)
- 30-45 min outdoor walk
- 10 min mobility flow (hips, thoracic spine, ankles)

### Week-by-week progression:
- **Week 1:** Teach and explore loads. Keep RPE 6.
- **Week 2:** Add a set to compound lifts (4 working sets). Increase walk to 35 min.
- **Week 3:** Increase loads ~5%. RPE 7.
- **Week 4:** Deload — drop one set off each exercise, focus on tempo (3-sec eccentric). Reassess weight, waist, BP, glucose patterns.

---

# PHASE 2: BUILD (Weeks 5–8)

Goal: Increase training density, introduce metabolic finishers, and start manipulating substrate use to improve insulin sensitivity.

### Resistance Session A (Mon & Fri)
- Back squat — 4 x 8
- DB incline press — 4 x 8
- Chest-supported row — 4 x 10
- DB RDL — 3 x 10
- Cable woodchop — 3 x 10/side
- **Finisher:** Kettlebell swing 4 x 15 (60 sec rest)

### Resistance Session B (Wed)
- Trap-bar deadlift — 4 x 6
- Standing DB press — 4 x 8
- Lat pulldown — 4 x 10
- Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8/side
- Hanging knee raise — 3 x 10
- **Finisher:** Sled push or loaded carry — 4 rounds, 20m

Rest 75-90 sec compounds, 60 sec accessories. RPE 7-8.

### Cardio Sessions
- **Tue: Zone 2** — 35-40 min, HR 60-70% max (~105-125 bpm for her age). This is the sweet spot for mitochondrial adaptation and insulin sensitivity.
- **Sat: Intervals** — Begin to introduce: 5 min warm-up, then 6 x (1 min moderate-hard / 2 min easy), 5 min cool-down. Bike or rower preferred (lower joint impact).

### Week-by-week progression:
- **Week 5:** Establish loads at prescribed reps.
- **Week 6:** Add load (~2.5-5kg compounds).
- **Week 7:** Push to top-end RPE 8. Increase intervals to 8 rounds.
- **Week 8:** Deload — reduce volume 40%, maintain intensity. Body comp/waist re-measurement.

---

# PHASE 3: INTENSIFY (Weeks 9–12)

Goal: Maximise glycaemic impact via HIIT, push body recomposition, peak the programme.

### Resistance Session A (Mon & Fri) — Lower Bias
- Back squat — 4 x 6 (RPE 8)
- Hip thrust — 4 x 8
- Walking lunge — 3 x 10/side
- Leg curl — 3 x 12
- DB chest press — 3 x 10
- Cable row — 3 x 12
- **Finisher:** 4 rounds — 12 KB swings + 10 goblet squats, 60 sec rest

### Resistance Session B (Wed) — Upper Bias
- Trap-bar deadlift — 4 x 5
- DB bench press — 4 x 8
- Lat pulldown — 4 x 10
- Seated row — 3 x 10
- DB shoulder press — 3 x 10
- Plank — 3 x 45 sec
- **Finisher:** Assault bike — 6 x 20 sec hard / 40 sec easy

### Cardio Sessions
- **Tue: Zone 2** — 40-45 min
- **Sat: HIIT** — 10 x (30 sec hard / 90 sec easy) on bike or rower. **Always finish with 5-min easy cool-down to clear lactate and avoid post-exercise hyperglycaemia from adrenaline spike.**

### Week-by-week progression:
- **Week 9:** Introduce loads, learn HIIT pacing.
- **Week 10:** Increase HIIT to 12 rounds.
- **Week 11:** Peak week — push compounds to RPE 8-9, top sets.
- **Week 12:** Light deload week (volume down 30%), retest baselines: waist, weight, body fat, blood pressure, and bloods (HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids if possible).

---

# NUTRITION PROTOCOL

The nutrition is honestly going to drive 60-70% of the glycaemic and fat loss results here. Here's how I'd structure it:

### Calorie & Macro Framework
Estimated maintenance ~1,900-2,100 kcal (will vary by activity/lean mass).

- **Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4):** Maintenance to small deficit (-200 kcal). Focus on food quality, not restriction. Habit-building.
- **Phase 2 (Weeks 5-8):** Moderate deficit (-400 to -500 kcal).
- **Phase 3 (Weeks 9-12):** Maintain deficit; add 1-2 higher carb refeed days around hardest training to support performance.

**Macro split (all phases):**
- **Protein:** 1.8-2.2 g/kg bodyweight — critical for satiety, lean mass retention, and lower glycaemic load of meals
- **Carbs:** 35-40% of calories (~120-180g/day) — quality and timing are the key, not just amount
- **Fat:** 30-35% of calories — emphasise mono- and polyunsaturated

### Carbohydrate Strategy (this is where glycaemic control lives)

1. **Low-GI, high-fibre sources only:** Lentils, chickpeas, black beans, steel-cut oats, quinoa, barley, sweet potato, berries, non-tropical fruit. Minimise/eliminate: white bread, white rice, sugary drinks, fruit juice, pastries, ultra-processed snacks.

2. **Carbohydrate timing:** Concentrate the day's carbs around training (the meal before and after). Lower carbs at breakfast and at evening meals — this aligns with diurnal insulin sensitivity patterns.

3. **The 30g fibre/day target:** Massive impact on glycaemic variability. Track this for the first 4 weeks.

4. **Vinegar trick:** 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar in water before higher-carb meals has good evidence for blunting postprandial glucose spikes.

5. **Meal sequencing:** Veg/protein first, carbs last. This reliably reduces glucose excursions.

### Protein Targets
~130-145g/day for her. Distribute across 4 meals (~30-40g per meal). Sources: chicken, fish, lean beef, eggs, Greek yogurt, tofu, tempeh, cottage cheese, whey shakes.

### Sample Daily Structure (Training Day)

- **Breakfast (lower carb):** 3-egg omelette with spinach, mushrooms, feta. Side of berries. Black coffee.
- **Lunch (moderate carb):** Grilled chicken (150g), large mixed salad with olive oil/vinegar, ½ cup quinoa, avocado.
- **Pre-workout (1-1.5 hr before):** Greek yogurt (200g) with 1 tbsp mixed nuts and ½ banana.
- **Post-workout:** Whey shake (30g) + apple.
- **Dinner:** Baked salmon (150g), roasted non-starchy veg (broccoli, peppers, courgette), small sweet potato.

### Non-Training Day Adjustment
Drop pre/post workout carbs. Replace with extra protein + veg meal. ~100-120g carbs total.

### Walking After Meals — Non-Negotiable Habit
10-15 minutes of walking after the largest meal of the day (typically dinner). The data on this for T2D is excellent — it can drop postprandial glucose by 20-30%. This is probably the single most impactful behavioural change after exercise itself.

### Alcohol
Limit to 2-3 drinks per week max, never on an empty stomach (hypo risk on metformin), and avoid sugary mixers.

### Hydration & Electrolytes
3L water/day. Add a pinch of salt and lemon if she's sweating heavily — important as glucose excretion can affect electrolyte balance.

---

# RECOVERY & MONITORING

- **Sleep:** Target 7-8 hours. Poor sleep destroys insulin sensitivity — track it. Even one bad night raises fasting glucose noticeably.
- **Stress management:** Cortisol drives glucose up. Encourage 5-10 min daily breathwork or short meditation.
- **Weekly check-ins:** Weight (same day, same time, weekly average not single reading), waist measurement, energy levels, sleep quality, fasting glucose patterns.
- **Monthly:** Photos, full body measurements, body fat (calipers or InBody), strength PRs.
- **End of Week 12:** Retest HbA1c with GP. Realistic target: 6.3-6.7% (from 7.2). Combined with the typical fat loss (~6-9kg if she's adherent), her metformin dose may even be reviewed.

# Quick Coaching Notes for You

- For the first two weeks, train her at the same time of day to get consistent glucose readings.
- Watch for **delayed hypos** post-evening training — happens up to 12 hours later. If she trains in the evening, make sure dinner has adequate carbs and protein.
- If she ever feels shaky, sweaty (beyond normal), dizzy, or confused during a session — **stop, test, treat.** Don't push through.
- This programme is intentionally conservative on impact and intensity in Phase 1. Many T2D clients have de-conditioned tendons/joints and the most common reason programmes fail is early injury.
